data.name: Devmanansh
data.short_meaning: God of Gods, Lord of Lords
data.long_meaning: Devmanansh is a compound name derived from the Sanskrit words ‘Deva’ meaning God and ‘Manas’ meaning mind or intellect. This name signifies the God of Gods or the Lord of Lords, who is the supreme being and the ruler of all minds and intellects.

in_sanskrit.name: देवमानंश
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The one born of or given by the Gods. Deva means God and Manas means mind. Māna means thinking and Nāsh means born.

in_hindi.name: देवमानंश
in_hindi.long_meaning: देव (God) से उत्पन्न (born) या देवोंसे मिला (given) हुआ।

in_tamil.name: திவமானான்ஷ்

in_telugu.name: దేవమానంశ్

data.cultural_impact: Devmanansh is a name deeply rooted in Hindu culture, emphasizing the reverence and devotion for the supreme deity. In ancient Hindu scriptures, God is often depicted as the ultimate consciousness and wisdom. Devmanansh's name is a daily reminder of this essential aspect of Hindu philosophy, encouraging devotees to seek and connect with the divine within themselves.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Devmanansh holds immense spiritual significance, as it represents the connection between the supreme consciousness (Deva) and the human intellect or mind (Manas). This name signifies the journey towards self-realization and union with the divine, reminding us that the ultimate source of wisdom and knowledge lies within the guiding grace of God. By invoking this name, one can foster a constant awareness and longing for the divine, which in turn can lead to inner peace and enlightenment.

historical_references.reference: The name 'Devmanansh' is derived from 'Deva' meaning god and 'Manansh' meaning intellect or thought. It is believed that this name emerged during the medieval period when Hindu philosophers and scholars were deeply engaged in the study and contemplation of divine knowledge and scriptures.

Another reference to the name 'Devmanansh' can be found in the Puranic literature, specifically the Skanda Purana. In this text, 'Devmanansh' is described as a divine being who was born to help Lord Shiva in his battle against the demon Tripurasura. He is also known as 'Skanda' or 'Kartikeya' and is revered as the god of war and knowledge.
